title: RWB-AD-019 in rwb-case: login name, edge composite route, source-data read shape and contract placement not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-019); WP B-P3-05; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 29, 41 and 44
description: The legacy story names no endpoint and no service, so the split into rwb-case leaves four values open: the per-service login name used by the console reads; the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-45 (path, merge rules, per-call timeout ownership); the path, paging and field shape of the rwb-source-data reconciliation read (REC-01 to REC-05) and of its business-key resolution read for REC-05, where Architecture v5 names only GET /freshness, GET /customers/{id}, GET /accounts/{id}, GET /collateral/{id}, GET /payments?accountId= and POST /business-days/{date}/ready; and the contract placement of the three console read operations, because the plan carries no contract story for RWB-AD-019. The 15-minute stale-set refresh cadence is a design value and is also open. The legacy story also places the console in the P1 Recovery data engine module, while this slice delivers the screen in rwb-case and leaves the reconciliation run and the freshness stamps with rwb-source-data.
evidence: RWB-AD-019 section 3 'Endpoints': 'No endpoint in this story.'; RWB-AD-019 metadata Module: P1 Recovery data engine; Architecture v5 slide 15 rwb-source-data REST IN list has no reconciliation or key-resolution operation; Architecture v5 slide 29 fixes schema rwb_case and its own login but the story-level login name is not agreed; Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-04 owner rwb-source-data); split_plan.json RWB-AD-019 slices RWB-P1-AD019-APP, RWB-P3-AD019-APP, RWB-P1-AD019-OPS, RWB-ITG-AD019-ITG with no CON slice
proposed: Publish the three console read operations under the rwb-case service contract; name the rwb-case login with the ACE DB owners; fix the SCR-45 composite route with the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON; add the reconciliation, key-resolution and freshness operations to the rwb-source-data contract as GET operations with the business date as a query parameter and a paged answer; keep the reconciliation run and the freshness stamps with rwb-source-data and the screen with rwb-case

title: rwb-case credit approval: login, edge route and the NLEADS and treatment contract shapes are not specified
source: WP B-P3-05; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.33 and its change note; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3; legacy RWB-E2-006; Ownership Map v1
description: No source gives the rwb-case login name (DP-02), the gateway-bff composite route and screen fields of SCR-14 (DP-19), the operation and field shape of the NLEADS credit-decision read that FSD P3 v4 places on v_ace_credit_decision through rwb-source-data, or the JSON field names of the rwb-treatment contract that return the plan terms and the legacy treatment result columns nleads_ref, credit_result, credit_result_reason and credit_result_at. The legacy story also records approval level L5 in AC2 against a Background that sets the plan at L6 or higher, and refuses level L6 in AC7 for a plan that needs L5; both values are copied unchanged and the level check itself is carried by the P2 story of the legacy key. The story is written with the rwb-case login named only by its role, the pack served case-side, and the missing contract shapes named as placeholders.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 12 gives GET /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-pack and POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result with a CreditResult body and no service login; FSD P3 v4 A2.33 lists v_ace_credit_decision as the integration point without an operation or fields; Ownership Map v1 keeps both treatment-scoped operations with rwb-integration (P2) and the DoA table with rwb-access (P4); no document names the SCR-14 composite route or the treatment contract field names
proposed: Agree the rwb-case login with the ACE DB story, the SCR-14 composite route with the edge story, the NLEADS credit-decision read and the treatment result fields with the P1 and S2 contract stories, and settle the approval-level values of AC2 and AC7 against doa.txt item 2.1.1 before wave 2 build starts

title: rwb-case booking confirmation: login, composite route, treatment booking fields, match-result shape and route-rule evaluator owner are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 3, 10, 12 and 13; FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.34; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 and T5; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 18
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 12.2 and 12.5 Contract; section 13 Solution plan; section 15 Screens and states
description: Five values the rwb-case slice needs are absent or unresolved in the sources. (1) The per-service database login for rwb-case is named nowhere; the story uses the phrase 'the rwb-case login (DP-02)' as a placeholder. (2) The gateway-bff composite route behind SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-01 My work has no field list, hop list or masking detail (DP-19). (3) The rwb-treatment contract response is not specified field by field, so which booking fields it returns (treatment type, state, booked at, booking difference) is a read, not a source value. (4) The booking-match result that rwb-integration passes to the rwb-case raiseTask activity has no published shape beyond the legacy TaskApi signature (caseId, taskCode, ownerRole, messageId, params), so the outcome, the accounts not booked and the difference terms are not typed anywhere. (5) The Temporal and Drools design puts the RESTRUCTURE, SETTLEMENT and BOOKING_MATCH route sets in rwb-treatment (slide 18), while the legacy flow step 6 and the case record ownership put the route-state move and R-RES-22/R-SET-13 in rwb-case; the story reads the case move as rwb-case work and the treatment state as rwb-treatment work, and the overlap of the approved package copies is left for the build to confirm.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 3 and section 10 name no login; section 12 lists the endpoints and the Java TaskApi methods but no result payload; section 13 names no screen route. Arch v5 slide 14 gives rwb-case the case and CMMN state and TreatmentBooked as an IN event; slide 44 puts JOB-08 in rwb-payment as an event-started workflow; TSD P3 T-A lists /api/recovery/v1 endpoints only. Temporal and Drools design slide 18 lists 'BOOKING_MATCH: booking confirmed' under S2 rwb-treatment, which is the overlap recorded here.
area: rwb-case contract, configuration and screen composition
proposed: Fix the rwb-case login in the platform DB story, publish the composite route and the treatment booking fields with RWB-P2-E2007-CON and the S2 contract, and publish the raiseTask result schema with the same contract; confirm in the build that rwb-case evaluates the route rows of its own approved copy while rwb-treatment applies the treatment state.

title: Case-fact read shape, cut-off rule and the reporting hand-off are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 4, 7 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (queue_measure); FSD P3 v4 A2.18; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 15
description: The sources do not fix (a) the case-fact response shape and the ageing, stage and queue dimension fields behind the dashboard, (b) the cut-off rule that decides which open cases belong to a business date, (c) the transport that carries the case-fact count to rwb-reporting at the 01:30 measure run: Architecture v5 slide 13 gives rwb-reporting an event subscription to rwb-case only, while legacy RWB-E2-009 section 12 calls a P3 interface in process, (d) the queue_measure dimension set (DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030), (e) the gateway-bff composite route detail for SCR-37, and (f) the rwb-case login name. The draft uses the read recorded in ASM-B-P3-05-E2009-101 to -105.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-009 section 12 lists CaseReportingApi.caseFacts and openCaseCount with no response schema; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 defines queue_measure with no dimension list; Architecture v5 slide 15 gives rwb-reporting events plus a source-data snapshot and slide 13 marks rwb-reporting as an event listener of rwb-case; no source names the rwb-case login or the SCR-37 route.
proposed: Agree the case-fact read schema, the cut-off rule and the fact transport with the rwb-reporting owner, then record the case-fact event projection in the case CON story and the Service Contract Catalog.

title: The case-side approval task shape, the approval-to-case status mapping, the escalation signal, the composite route and the rwb-case login are not specified in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14, 25 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 24 and the workflow kit note); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md (T3.1 task and timer, T3.2 lists, appendix T-A); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 013 Approval routing with the delegation of authority table v1.md (sections 4, 11 and 13)
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.4; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: Architecture v5 gives rwb-decision the approval (ApprovalWorkflow of the kit, approvals table in rwb_decision) and the events ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided and RulePackageInForce on rwb.decision.events.v1, and rwb-case the case, its tasks and its timers with GET /tasks and POST /tasks/{id}/complete. No source states which fields of an approval request or a decision reach the case, so the payload that opens the decision task has no agreed shape. TSD P3 v3 T3.1 gives the task columns task_code, element_type, owner_role, due_at, status, completed_at and outcome_code and no column of its own for the approval reference, the preparer reference or the approval level, and T3.2 gives DECISION_TASK and WAITING_APPROVAL as list values only. No source states which case status accompanies the state a routing rule names on a refusal, nor what a case does while an approval is held as HELD_NO_LIMIT with no approver named. No source defines an escalation event on rwb.decision.events.v1, so the case cannot know from the published event list how an escalated approval reaches it. No source names the rwb-case login (DP-02) and no source fixes the gateway-bff composite route and field list that serve the waiting-approval case and the decision task (DP-19). The two activities, the task projection and the case read cannot be built and tested without these defaults.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14: rwb-decision IN POST /approvals/{id}/decide and OUT topic rwb.decision.events.v1 ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce; slide 41: rwb-decision owns approvals, central decision ledger and DMN model registry, rwb-case owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation and timers; slide 25 note: ApprovalWorkflow on rwb-decision, routed by authority (DoA). TSD P3 v3 T3.1 task (DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026) and timer (DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-044); T3.2 LOV-ELEMENT DECISION_TASK and LOV-CASE-STATUS WAITING_APPROVAL; appendix T-A API-P3-002, API-P3-008 and API-P3-009. Legacy RWB-E2-013 section 4 step 4 asks P3 to open the decision task and start the service level timer through the P3 interfaces, section 11 lists DF-WRK-019, DF-WRK-020, DF-WRK-023, DF-WRK-030 and DF-WRK-032 as writes through those interfaces, and section 13 leaves the timer to JOB-05. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02, DP-10 and DP-19 name the per-service login, the workflow kit and the gateway-bff route but no value.
area: Case state, approval task and event mapping
proposed: Fix the case-side defaults at the RWB-P7-E2013-CON contract review and the RWB-PLT-N001-CON review: the approval event fields the case consumes and the task fields it writes (approval reference and preparer reference included), the escalation representation, the approval-status-to-case-status mapping, the composite route field list, and the rwb-case login name from the ACE DB naming decision. Record the outcome in the contract and in the case DB story; no business value changes.
